recovery_note: Exact 190-writer seed recovered from this Literature chat’s 3 October command record; originally saved only to /private/tmp. Not a completed source-verified candidate list.

candidates.name: Adonis
candidates.works: Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses
candidates.rationale: Remade Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and a sustained dialogue with inherited forms.
candidates.reservation: The case rests chiefly on poetry and requires close assessment across translations.

candidates.name: Ibrahim al-Koni
candidates.works: Gold Dust; The Bleeding of the Stone
candidates.rationale: A desert cosmology joins Tuareg experience, ecological limits and metaphysical fiction.
candidates.reservation: The symbolic system can be difficult to assess through a small translated sample.

candidates.name: Ibrahim Nasrallah
candidates.works: Time of White Horses; The Second War of the Dog
candidates.rationale: A large narrative project reconstructs Palestinian history alongside speculative and lyrical writing.
candidates.reservation: The strongest case needs to establish the formal achievement across the wider oeuvre.

candidates.name: Hoda Barakat
candidates.works: The Stone of Laughter; The Night Mail
candidates.rationale: Unstable voices and fractured communities turn displacement into a distinctive narrative form.
candidates.reservation: A relatively compact translated corpus makes breadth harder to compare.

candidates.name: Hanan al-Shaykh
candidates.works: The Story of Zahra; Women of Sand and Myrrh
candidates.rationale: Women’s voices expose the intimate workings of war, migration and social constraint.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to distinguish the literary case from thematic importance alone.

candidates.name: Sahar Khalifeh
candidates.works: Wild Thorns; The Inheritance
candidates.rationale: A sustained Palestinian feminist oeuvre connects national struggle with class and domestic power.
candidates.reservation: Translation coverage is uneven across a substantial career.

candidates.name: Ghassan Zaqtan
candidates.works: Like a Straw Bird It Follows Me; Describing the Past
candidates.rationale: A restrained poetics of traces and absence transforms Palestinian memory into oblique lyric form.
candidates.reservation: International visibility remains narrower than that of several prose contenders.

candidates.name: Nuruddin Farah
candidates.works: Maps; Secrets
candidates.rationale: A long sequence of novels interrogates state power, kinship and exile through shifting perspectives.
candidates.reservation: A final case should identify the most distinctive formal achievement within a very broad oeuvre.

candidates.name: Mia Couto
candidates.works: Sleepwalking Land; Confession of the Lioness
candidates.rationale: Linguistic invention brings oral storytelling into novels of war, memory and postcolonial life.
candidates.reservation: Wordplay and oral registers are particularly sensitive to translation.

candidates.name: Boubacar Boris Diop
candidates.works: Murambi: The Book of Bones; Doomi Golo
candidates.rationale: Historical witness and writing in Wolof challenge both political violence and linguistic hierarchy.
candidates.reservation: The strongest comparison needs access to the Wolof as well as French work.

candidates.name: Ananda Devi
candidates.works: Eve Out of Her Ruins; Indian Tango
candidates.rationale: Intense narrative voices explore violence, caste, gender and marginal lives in Mauritius and beyond.
candidates.reservation: An assessment should establish sustained formal range beyond the best-known novels.

candidates.name: Scholastique Mukasonga
candidates.works: Our Lady of the Nile; The Barefoot Woman
candidates.rationale: Fiction and memorial prose recover social worlds destroyed by the Rwandan genocide.
candidates.reservation: The case must articulate literary innovation as well as the force of testimony.

candidates.name: Véronique Tadjo
candidates.works: The Shadow of Imana; In the Company of Men
candidates.rationale: Polyphonic narrative and fable connect collective memory, violence and ecological interdependence.
candidates.reservation: A multilingual reading of the wider oeuvre would strengthen the comparison.

candidates.name: Ben Okri
candidates.works: The Famished Road; Astonishing the Gods
candidates.rationale: Visionary fiction makes spirit worlds and material deprivation coexist in an original narrative register.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to weigh the whole career beyond the breakthrough novel.

candidates.name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
candidates.works: Half of a Yellow Sun; Americanah
candidates.rationale: Historical and diasporic novels render race, migration and social power through intimate lives.
candidates.reservation: A shorter career than many contenders leaves the lifetime-achievement comparison open.

candidates.name: Tsitsi Dangarembga
candidates.works: Nervous Conditions; This Mournable Body
candidates.rationale: A connected novel sequence traces the psychic costs of colonialism, gender and class.
candidates.reservation: The concentrated fictional corpus offers less genre breadth than some alternatives.

candidates.name: Zoë Wicomb
candidates.works: You Can’t Get Lost in Cape Town; David’s Story
candidates.rationale: Fragmented narrative dismantles racial classification and inherited accounts of resistance.
candidates.reservation: The formally complex, relatively small corpus calls for careful comparative reading.

candidates.name: Antjie Krog
candidates.works: Country of My Skull; Lady Anne
candidates.rationale: Poetry and literary witness test the language of guilt, reconciliation and belonging.
candidates.reservation: The English nonfiction should not eclipse the Afrikaans poetry in evaluation.

candidates.name: Ivan Vladislavić
candidates.works: The Restless Supermarket; Portrait with Keys
candidates.rationale: Fragmented urban narratives make language and the built environment register historical change.
candidates.reservation: International recognition is less extensive than the achievement merits; close reading is essential.

candidates.name: Leila Aboulela
candidates.works: The Translator; Minaret
candidates.rationale: Interior narratives of migration and faith broaden the moral vocabulary of the English novel.
candidates.reservation: The case requires a clear account of formal distinctiveness across the oeuvre.

candidates.name: Alain Mabanckou
candidates.works: Broken Glass; Memoirs of a Porcupine
candidates.rationale: Oral energy, satire and unconventional narration recast postcolonial and diasporic experience.
candidates.reservation: A final argument should weigh sustained achievement beyond exuberant narrative voice.

candidates.name: Abdellatif Laâbi
candidates.works: The Bottom of the Jar; Beyond the Hand
candidates.rationale: A long poetic and autobiographical career joins linguistic invention with imprisonment and exile.
candidates.reservation: The bilingual oeuvre requires broader reading than its limited English reception.

candidates.name: Tahar Ben Jelloun
candidates.works: The Sand Child; This Blinding Absence of Light
candidates.rationale: Gendered storytelling and narratives of incarceration examine the instability of social identity.
candidates.reservation: The unevenness of a prolific oeuvre should be assessed directly.

candidates.name: Anne Carson
candidates.works: Autobiography of Red; Nox
candidates.rationale: Hybrid works remake the boundaries between classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual form.
candidates.reservation: The experimental corpus resists conventional comparisons of genre and scale.

candidates.name: Margaret Atwood
candidates.works: The Handmaid’s Tale; Alias Grace
candidates.rationale: A large, versatile oeuvre examines gender, power and ecological danger through narrative invention.
candidates.reservation: Public prominence should not substitute for comparing the full literary achievement.

candidates.name: Michael Ondaatje
candidates.works: The English Patient; Anil’s Ghost
candidates.rationale: Lyrical fragmentation connects private lives with war, migration and unstable historical records.
candidates.reservation: The case must balance the poetry with the more widely known fiction.

candidates.name: Dionne Brand
candidates.works: A Map to the Door of No Return; Ossuaries
candidates.rationale: Poetry and essay unsettle the languages of diaspora, slavery and belonging.
candidates.reservation: The formally demanding corpus has less international exposure than some peers.

candidates.name: Jamaica Kincaid
candidates.works: Annie John; A Small Place
candidates.rationale: A sharp narrative voice links colonial power, family intimacy and landscape.
candidates.reservation: A relatively concentrated oeuvre requires attention to its range across genres.

candidates.name: Edwidge Danticat
candidates.works: The Farming of Bones; Brother, I’m Dying
candidates.rationale: Fiction and memoir make Haitian history and migration legible through intimate, interlinked lives.
candidates.reservation: A citation should distinguish narrative achievement from the importance of its subject.

candidates.name: Don DeLillo
candidates.works: White Noise; Underworld
candidates.rationale: A distinctive prose examines media, technology, mass culture and historical consciousness.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to assess the later work alongside the canonical middle period.

candidates.name: Thomas Pynchon
candidates.works: Gravity’s Rainbow; Mason & Dixon
candidates.rationale: Encyclopedic fiction links systems of power, scientific knowledge and countercultural imagination.
candidates.reservation: Density and uneven accessibility complicate comparative reading across the whole oeuvre.

candidates.name: Joyce Carol Oates
candidates.works: them; Blonde
candidates.rationale: An exceptionally large oeuvre maps violence, class and gender through varied narrative forms.
candidates.reservation: The scale and unevenness of the corpus make selection of representative work consequential.

candidates.name: Marilynne Robinson
candidates.works: Housekeeping; Gilead
candidates.rationale: Meditative prose and moral interiority bring theology, family and American history into dialogue.
candidates.reservation: The small number of novels makes the breadth of the achievement a comparative question.

candidates.name: Louise Erdrich
candidates.works: Love Medicine; The Night Watchman
candidates.rationale: Interlinked Indigenous narratives join communal memory, legal power and inventive storytelling.
candidates.reservation: The full multivolume project needs evaluation beyond its recent prize-winning books.

candidates.name: Maxine Hong Kingston
candidates.works: The Woman Warrior; China Men
candidates.rationale: Hybrid autobiography and myth transformed the representation of migration and inherited stories.
candidates.reservation: Genre boundaries and a concentrated core corpus require a precise literary case.

candidates.name: Richard Powers
candidates.works: The Gold Bug Variations; The Overstory
candidates.rationale: Formally ambitious novels connect scientific systems with emotional and ecological life.
candidates.reservation: The balance between conceptual exposition and fictional force merits scrutiny.

candidates.name: Percival Everett
candidates.works: Erasure; The Trees
candidates.rationale: Genre shifts, satire and philosophical play expose the structures of racial representation.
candidates.reservation: Recent visibility should be weighed against the breadth of a much longer career.

candidates.name: George Saunders
candidates.works: Tenth of December; Lincoln in the Bardo
candidates.rationale: Inventive voices and speculative situations turn moral pressure into new short-story and novel forms.
candidates.reservation: The comparatively recent novel-length work leaves a chiefly short-fiction case.

candidates.name: Colson Whitehead
candidates.works: The Underground Railroad; The Nickel Boys
candidates.rationale: Historical reinvention and genre experimentation illuminate American institutions and racial violence.
candidates.reservation: The lifetime-achievement comparison remains open against longer-established writers.

candidates.name: Edward P. Jones
candidates.works: The Known World; All Aunt Hagar’s Children
candidates.rationale: Layered narration gives Black communities and the history of slavery unusual moral complexity.
candidates.reservation: The small published corpus is the principal comparative limitation.

candidates.name: Alice Walker
candidates.works: The Color Purple; Meridian
candidates.rationale: A multigenre oeuvre reshaped the representation of Black women’s interior lives and collective struggle.
candidates.reservation: Assessment needs to consider the wider career beyond the dominant landmark novel.

candidates.name: John Edgar Wideman
candidates.works: Philadelphia Fire; Brothers and Keepers
candidates.rationale: Experimental narration connects family history, incarceration and the public record of race.
candidates.reservation: The dispersed, formally demanding oeuvre has a less unified international reception.

candidates.name: Lydia Davis
candidates.works: The Collected Stories of Lydia Davis; Can’t and Won’t
candidates.rationale: Extreme compression and linguistic precision expanded what a short story can do.
candidates.reservation: The miniature form requires comparison without equating length with achievement.

candidates.name: William T. Vollmann
candidates.works: Europe Central; Rising Up and Rising Down
candidates.rationale: Large narrative and documentary projects investigate violence, ethics and marginal experience.
candidates.reservation: The enormous, uneven corpus is difficult to assess comprehensively.

candidates.name: Yusef Komunyakaa
candidates.works: Dien Cai Dau; Neon Vernacular
candidates.rationale: Musical language and sensory precision transform war and racial history into sustained lyric achievement.
candidates.reservation: An international comparison requires attention to a primarily American reception.

candidates.name: Rita Dove
candidates.works: Thomas and Beulah; Sonata Mulattica
candidates.rationale: Poetic sequences connect intimate lives with the historical erasure of Black experience.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to assess formal range across the complete poetry.

candidates.name: Jorie Graham
candidates.works: The Dream of the Unified Field; Sea Change
candidates.rationale: Syntax and perception become instruments for confronting time, embodiment and ecological crisis.
candidates.reservation: Her demanding poetics divide readers and depend heavily on close reading.

candidates.name: Susan Howe
candidates.works: My Emily Dickinson; That This
candidates.rationale: Archival fragments and visual arrangements remake relations between history and poetic voice.
candidates.reservation: Page design and linguistic texture complicate translation and comparative evaluation.

candidates.name: Charles Wright
candidates.works: Black Zodiac; The World of the Ten Thousand Things
candidates.rationale: A sustained meditative poetry joins landscape, memory and metaphysical questioning.
candidates.reservation: The case needs to establish international significance beyond domestic honors.

candidates.name: Joy Harjo
candidates.works: She Had Some Horses; An American Sunrise
candidates.rationale: Poetry joins Muscogee memory, music and survivance in a distinctive contemporary voice.
candidates.reservation: Institutional prominence should be separated from a close assessment of poetic innovation.

candidates.name: Mei-mei Berssenbrugge
candidates.works: Empathy; A Treatise on Stars
candidates.rationale: Long-line experimental poetry explores perception, relation and the boundaries of the human.
candidates.reservation: The specialized poetic reception makes a broader comparative case necessary.

candidates.name: Ian McEwan
candidates.works: Atonement; Saturday
candidates.rationale: Precise narrative structures expose the moral consequences of misreading, desire and historical contingency.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to distinguish sustained innovation from literary prestige.

candidates.name: Julian Barnes
candidates.works: Flaubert’s Parrot; The Sense of an Ending
candidates.rationale: Playful structures and unreliable memory connect literary history with ordinary ethical failure.
candidates.reservation: The case rests on subtle tonal and structural achievements rather than a single defining innovation.

candidates.name: John Banville
candidates.works: The Book of Evidence; The Sea
candidates.rationale: Highly worked prose and unreliable narrators turn memory and aesthetic perception into moral problems.
candidates.reservation: Stylistic brilliance needs to be weighed against the range of the wider oeuvre.

candidates.name: Colm Tóibín
candidates.works: The Master; Brooklyn
candidates.rationale: Restrained narration makes exile, family and unspoken feeling central to historical and contemporary fiction.
candidates.reservation: A final case should specify formal achievement beyond thematic consistency.

candidates.name: Sebastian Barry
candidates.works: The Secret Scripture; Days Without End
candidates.rationale: Musical voices recover lives obscured by Irish and transatlantic history.
candidates.reservation: The comparison should encompass drama and poetry as well as the best-known novels.

candidates.name: Caryl Churchill
candidates.works: Top Girls; Far Away
candidates.rationale: Radical theatrical forms reconfigure time, identity and political argument on stage.
candidates.reservation: Drama needs assessment through performance as well as translated scripts.

candidates.name: Paul Muldoon
candidates.works: Moy Sand and Gravel; Meeting the British
candidates.rationale: Virtuosic rhyme and associative structures join historical violence with linguistic play.
candidates.reservation: Formal ingenuity and emotional force require careful comparison across collections.

candidates.name: Ali Smith
candidates.works: How to Be Both; Autumn
candidates.rationale: Playful structures and narrative voices respond to art, time and contemporary social fracture.
candidates.reservation: The committee should test the durability of work closely tied to current events.

candidates.name: Jeanette Winterson
candidates.works: Oranges Are Not the Only Fruit; Written on the Body
candidates.rationale: Innovative narratives unsettle inherited categories of gender, sexuality and selfhood.
candidates.reservation: The career’s range and uneven critical reception call for a selective but fair reading.

candidates.name: Pat Barker
candidates.works: Regeneration; The Silence of the Girls
candidates.rationale: Historical fiction scrutinizes war, trauma and the voices excluded from heroic narratives.
candidates.reservation: The literary case should identify the formal contribution beyond historical recovery.

candidates.name: Bernardine Evaristo
candidates.works: Girl, Woman, Other; The Emperor’s Babe
candidates.rationale: Hybrid verse and polyphonic fiction expand the representation of Black British lives.
candidates.reservation: The comparison needs to extend beyond the recent breakthrough in international recognition.

candidates.name: Gerald Murnane
candidates.works: The Plains; Border Districts
candidates.rationale: A radically inward fiction builds distinctive systems of landscape, memory and mental images.
candidates.reservation: Its deliberately narrow aesthetic world may divide comparative judgments.

candidates.name: Alexis Wright
candidates.works: Carpentaria; The Swan Book
candidates.rationale: Large, polyphonic narratives remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time.
candidates.reservation: The culturally specific formal system requires informed reading rather than thematic shorthand.

candidates.name: David Malouf
candidates.works: Remembering Babylon; Ransom
candidates.rationale: Lyrical fiction and poetry explore encounters between cultures, bodily experience and historical memory.
candidates.reservation: The full poetry and short fiction should be weighed alongside the novels.

candidates.name: Peter Carey
candidates.works: Oscar and Lucinda; True History of the Kelly Gang
candidates.rationale: Inventive voices rework colonial history and the myths of Australian identity.
candidates.reservation: The committee needs to weigh the later oeuvre against the established landmark novels.

candidates.name: Tim Winton
candidates.works: Cloudstreet; Breath
candidates.rationale: Vernacular prose connects class, coastal environments and spiritual longing.
candidates.reservation: A strong regional achievement still needs a persuasive international comparison.

candidates.name: Patricia Grace
candidates.works: Potiki; Cousins
candidates.rationale: Māori communal voices and narrative structures challenge dominant accounts of land and identity.
candidates.reservation: The translated and international reception is narrower than the local significance.

candidates.name: Witi Ihimaera
candidates.works: The Whale Rider; Bulibasha
candidates.rationale: A substantial Māori oeuvre brings genealogy, community and cultural change into modern fiction.
candidates.reservation: The committee should establish literary range beyond the best-known adapted novel.

candidates.name: Can Xue
candidates.works: Frontier; Love in the New Millennium
candidates.rationale: Dreamlike narrative worlds destabilize ordinary psychology, space and causal storytelling.
candidates.reservation: The surrealist methods require sustained reading beyond a few translated works.

candidates.name: Yu Hua
candidates.works: To Live; Brothers
candidates.rationale: A changing narrative style brings ordinary survival into contact with extreme historical violence.
candidates.reservation: The contrast between restrained early work and broad later satire merits evaluation.

candidates.name: Yan Lianke
candidates.works: The Four Books; The Explosion Chronicles
candidates.rationale: Grotesque and mythic narrative forms expose the violence of ideology and development.
candidates.reservation: The comparison should assess formal invention independently of censorship and political visibility.

candidates.name: Su Tong
candidates.works: Raise the Red Lantern; The Boat to Redemption
candidates.rationale: Atmospheric prose examines desire, patriarchy and historical rupture through tightly controlled worlds.
candidates.reservation: English reception covers only part of a much larger oeuvre.

candidates.name: Wang Anyi
candidates.works: The Song of Everlasting Sorrow; Fu Ping
candidates.rationale: Detailed urban narratives give changing social worlds and women’s lives historical depth.
candidates.reservation: A fuller translated sample is needed to compare the range of the oeuvre.

candidates.name: Bei Dao
candidates.works: The August Sleepwalker; City Gate, Open Up
candidates.rationale: Compressed, oblique poetry transformed the language of modern Chinese lyric and exile.
candidates.reservation: The wider achievement should not be reduced to political symbolism.

candidates.name: Duo Duo
candidates.works: Words as Movement; The Boy Who Catches Wasps
candidates.rationale: A highly individual modernist lyric transforms historical rupture into dense verbal music.
candidates.reservation: Translation remains a substantial obstacle to comparison of the poetic texture.

candidates.name: Yang Lian
candidates.works: Narrative Poem; Concentric Circles
candidates.rationale: Long poetic structures join cultural memory, exile and formal experimentation.
candidates.reservation: The demanding architecture calls for more than a brief anthology-based assessment.

candidates.name: Li Ang
candidates.works: The Butcher’s Wife; The Lost Garden
candidates.rationale: Feminist fiction confronts sexual power and Taiwan’s social and political history.
candidates.reservation: International translation coverage is uneven across the career.

candidates.name: Haruki Murakami
candidates.works: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle; Kafka on the Shore
candidates.rationale: Recurring dream worlds and estranged narrators reshaped the international reach of Japanese fiction.
candidates.reservation: Global popularity does not settle debates over repetition and unevenness.

candidates.name: Yoko Tawada
candidates.works: The Emissary; Memoirs of a Polar Bear
candidates.rationale: Bilingual writing turns linguistic estrangement into inventive narrative and poetic forms.
candidates.reservation: Both language corpora need evaluation; one translated novel is insufficient.

candidates.name: Yoko Ogawa
candidates.works: The Memory Police; The Housekeeper and the Professor
candidates.rationale: Quietly unsettling narratives investigate memory, bodily vulnerability and control.
candidates.reservation: The extensive Japanese corpus is only partly represented in English.

candidates.name: Hiromi Kawakami
candidates.works: Strange Weather in Tokyo; The Nakano Thrift Shop
candidates.rationale: Understated and fantastical narratives expose oddness within everyday relations.
candidates.reservation: The comparative case needs to encompass the more experimental work.

candidates.name: Minae Mizumura
candidates.works: A True Novel; The Fall of Language in the Age of English
candidates.rationale: Formal reinvention of the Japanese novel connects literary inheritance with linguistic inequality.
candidates.reservation: The compact corpus makes the scale of the lifetime achievement a question.

candidates.name: Hwang Sok-yong
candidates.works: The Guest; Mater 2-10
candidates.rationale: A long fictional career recovers divided histories through layered voices and social worlds.
candidates.reservation: The literary argument should be distinguished from biography and political courage.

candidates.name: Kim Hyesoon
candidates.works: Autobiography of Death; Phantom Pain Wings
candidates.rationale: Radical bodily and spectral imagery reworks lyric voice through feminist and collective experience.
candidates.reservation: The case depends on assessing poetic innovation through several translations.

candidates.name: Ko Un
candidates.works: Ten Thousand Lives; Flowers of a Moment
candidates.rationale: A vast poetic project joins individual lives with Korea’s historical experience.
candidates.reservation: Public misconduct allegations are a reputational consideration; the literary corpus also needs selective assessment.

candidates.name: Bae Suah
candidates.works: Untold Night and Day; A Greater Music
candidates.rationale: Dislocated voices and temporal loops push Korean fiction toward musical and philosophical abstraction.
candidates.reservation: International translation covers a relatively small portion of the career.

candidates.name: Amitav Ghosh
candidates.works: The Glass Palace; Sea of Poppies
candidates.rationale: Historical novels and essays connect empire, migration and ecological crisis across the Indian Ocean.
candidates.reservation: The full literary case should distinguish fictional achievement from influential commentary.

candidates.name: Salman Rushdie
candidates.works: Midnight’s Children; The Satanic Verses
candidates.rationale: Verbal abundance and hybrid histories transformed the postcolonial novel’s narrative possibilities.
candidates.reservation: Political symbolism should not displace evaluation of a varied and uneven oeuvre.

candidates.name: Vikram Seth
candidates.works: A Suitable Boy; The Golden Gate
candidates.rationale: Large social narrative and technically inventive verse fiction join classical forms with modern lives.
candidates.reservation: The major works are few and widely spaced, making the breadth comparison consequential.

candidates.name: Arundhati Roy
candidates.works: The God of Small Things; The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
candidates.rationale: Inventive syntax and layered narrative connect intimate damage with caste, state power and history.
candidates.reservation: A relatively small novel corpus leaves a case partly dependent on literary nonfiction.

candidates.name: Rohinton Mistry
candidates.works: A Fine Balance; Family Matters
candidates.rationale: Socially expansive novels render ordinary lives under political pressure with moral complexity.
candidates.reservation: The limited number of published books makes sustained range a comparative question.

candidates.name: Geetanjali Shree
candidates.works: Tomb of Sand; The Empty Space
candidates.rationale: Playful, expansive Hindi prose unsettles borders of language, gender and historical memory.
candidates.reservation: International assessment should extend beyond the single breakthrough translation.

candidates.name: Perumal Murugan
candidates.works: One Part Woman; Poonachi
candidates.rationale: Rural voices and fable examine caste, sexuality and the coercion of ordinary life.
candidates.reservation: The case requires a broader Tamil corpus assessment beyond internationally prominent titles.

candidates.name: Jeyamohan
candidates.works: Vishnupuram; The White Elephant
candidates.rationale: Philosophical and historical fiction builds a large, ambitious Tamil narrative world.
candidates.reservation: Limited translation makes comparative evaluation unusually difficult.

candidates.name: K. Satchidanandan
candidates.works: While I Write; Misplaced Objects and Other Poems
candidates.rationale: A long poetic career joins modernist experimentation with ethical and multilingual engagement.
candidates.reservation: Translation and a dispersed bibliography complicate a representative assessment.

candidates.name: Mohsin Hamid
candidates.works: The Reluctant Fundamentalist; Exit West
candidates.rationale: Compact, formally inventive novels connect migration, global power and unstable identity.
candidates.reservation: A relatively small corpus leaves the lifetime-achievement comparison open.

candidates.name: Selina Hossain
candidates.works: Hangor Nodi Grenade; Gayatri Sandhya
candidates.rationale: A large Bengali oeuvre connects liberation history with women’s lives and social change.
candidates.reservation: Restricted international translation makes the formal comparison difficult.

candidates.name: Goenawan Mohamad
candidates.works: Selected Poems; Catatan Pinggir
candidates.rationale: Poetry and literary essays sustain a distinctive dialogue between freedom, history and cultural tradition.
candidates.reservation: A representative translated selection is needed to assess the large essay corpus.

candidates.name: Eka Kurniawan
candidates.works: Beauty Is a Wound; Man Tiger
candidates.rationale: Myth, grotesque humor and historical violence meet in formally energetic Indonesian fiction.
candidates.reservation: The internationally visible corpus remains smaller than that of many veteran contenders.

candidates.name: Seno Gumira Ajidarma
candidates.works: Eyewitness; Jazz, Perfume and the Incident
candidates.rationale: Experimental storytelling and documentary fragments confront repression and the instability of evidence.
candidates.reservation: Translation coverage is limited and complicates evaluation of the wider oeuvre.

candidates.name: Dương Thu Hương
candidates.works: Paradise of the Blind; Novel Without a Name
candidates.rationale: Fiction confronts war, disillusionment and moral survival through intimate narrative voices.
candidates.reservation: Political visibility must be weighed separately from sustained literary achievement.

candidates.name: Bảo Ninh
candidates.works: The Sorrow of War; Hà Nội at Midnight
candidates.rationale: Fragmented memory and lyrical narration unsettle heroic accounts of war.
candidates.reservation: The international case depends heavily on one novel; the stories need fuller reading.

candidates.name: Jessica Hagedorn
candidates.works: Dogeaters; The Gangster of Love
candidates.rationale: Collage and popular-culture voices connect dictatorship, migration and diasporic identity.
candidates.reservation: The case requires evaluation across fiction, performance and poetry.

candidates.name: Mahmoud Dowlatabadi
candidates.works: Kelidar; The Colonel
candidates.rationale: Large social narratives and concentrated tragic fiction explore rural change and political violence.
candidates.reservation: Much of the foundational Persian oeuvre is not readily available in English.

candidates.name: Shahrnush Parsipur
candidates.works: Women Without Men; Touba and the Meaning of Night
candidates.rationale: Mythic and experimental narratives recast women’s historical and spiritual experience.
candidates.reservation: Translation offers a limited view of the broader oeuvre.

candidates.name: Atiq Rahimi
candidates.works: Earth and Ashes; The Patience Stone
candidates.rationale: Spare, concentrated narratives connect war, silence and gendered power.
candidates.reservation: The literary corpus is comparatively compact and overlaps with a film career.

candidates.name: Bakhtiyar Ali
candidates.works: The Last Pomegranate Tree; I Stared at the Night of the City
candidates.rationale: Expansive, allegorical novels reimagine Kurdish history, violence and collective memory.
candidates.reservation: Limited translation remains a major barrier to fair comparative reading.

candidates.name: Latife Tekin
candidates.works: Dear Shameless Death; Berji Kristin: Tales from the Garbage Hills
candidates.rationale: Oral forms and collective voices transform rural migration and urban dispossession into narrative invention.
candidates.reservation: The English corpus represents only part of a sustained career.

candidates.name: Oya Baydar
candidates.works: The Lost Word; The General of the Garbage Dump
candidates.rationale: Fiction explores memory, ideological failure and social fragmentation through changing perspectives.
candidates.reservation: International recognition and translation are less extensive than the domestic oeuvre.

candidates.name: Elif Shafak
candidates.works: The Bastard of Istanbul; 10 Minutes 38 Seconds in This Strange World
candidates.rationale: Polyphonic novels connect gender, cultural inheritance and migration across languages.
candidates.reservation: Wide readership needs to be matched by a precise account of formal innovation.

candidates.name: Mircea Cărtărescu
candidates.works: Blinding; Solenoid
candidates.rationale: Visionary, densely patterned prose turns memory and the body into an expansive metaphysical project.
candidates.reservation: The scale and translation demands make selective reading a significant risk.

candidates.name: Péter Nádas
candidates.works: A Book of Memories; Parallel Stories
candidates.rationale: Complex structures of perception and embodiment connect private lives with European history.
candidates.reservation: The large, demanding corpus requires unusually substantial comparative reading.

candidates.name: László Végel
candidates.works: Memoirs of a Pimp; Neoplanta
candidates.rationale: A borderland oeuvre interrogates minority life, urban memory and historical displacement.
candidates.reservation: Limited international translation makes the broader achievement harder to assess.

candidates.name: Elena Ferrante
candidates.works: My Brilliant Friend; The Days of Abandonment
candidates.rationale: A sustained investigation of women’s friendship, class and selfhood reworks social narrative.
candidates.reservation: The public identity is unverified; practical award arrangements would require private resolution.

candidates.name: Claudio Magris
candidates.works: Danube; Microcosms
candidates.rationale: Hybrid travel, essay and fiction map Europe through borderlands, memory and intellectual history.
candidates.reservation: The achievement crosses genres and needs an explicit literary rather than scholarly comparison.

candidates.name: Dacia Maraini
candidates.works: The Silent Duchess; Bagheria
candidates.rationale: A long multigenre oeuvre examines women’s lives, silence and historical power.
candidates.reservation: The committee should assess the entire career beyond its most familiar novels.

candidates.name: Erri De Luca
candidates.works: God’s Mountain; The Day Before Happiness
candidates.rationale: Compressed prose brings labor, spiritual inheritance and historical experience into intimate narrative.
candidates.reservation: The restrained scale of individual works calls for evaluation across the full corpus.

candidates.name: Hélène Cixous
candidates.works: The Book of Promethea; The Third Body
candidates.rationale: Experimental writing dissolves boundaries between autobiography, philosophy and fiction.
candidates.reservation: Her theoretical influence should be separated from the literary achievement itself.

candidates.name: Pierre Michon
candidates.works: Small Lives; The Eleven
candidates.rationale: Dense, compressed prose transforms obscure lives and art history into powerful narrative inquiry.
candidates.reservation: A small core corpus raises questions of scale without diminishing literary intensity.

candidates.name: Pascal Quignard
candidates.works: All the World’s Mornings; The Roving Shadows
candidates.rationale: Fragmentary writing links music, memory and ancient texts in an unusually coherent cross-genre project.
candidates.reservation: The dispersal and learned texture of the oeuvre complicate representative reading.

candidates.name: Emmanuel Carrère
candidates.works: The Adversary; The Kingdom
candidates.rationale: Self-implicating documentary narratives explore belief, violence and the ethics of telling other lives.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to evaluate the ethical and formal limits of the narrator’s self-insertion.

candidates.name: Michel Houellebecq
candidates.works: The Elementary Particles; The Map and the Territory
candidates.rationale: Satirical novels diagnose commodified intimacy and social exhaustion through a distinctive narrative voice.
candidates.reservation: Provocation and public notoriety should not substitute for literary comparison.

candidates.name: Mathias Énard
candidates.works: Zone; Compass
candidates.rationale: Formally ambitious narratives connect Mediterranean histories, violence and cultural entanglement.
candidates.reservation: The strongest comparison should test the wider oeuvre beyond two major landmarks.

candidates.name: Marie NDiaye
candidates.works: Three Strong Women; My Heart Hemmed In
candidates.rationale: Uncanny narrative voices expose exclusion, family power and unstable belonging.
candidates.reservation: The translated sample remains incomplete across fiction and theatre.

candidates.name: Sylvie Germain
candidates.works: The Book of Nights; The Weeping Woman on the Streets of Prague
candidates.rationale: Mythic and lyrical fiction turns historical violence into a sustained inquiry into suffering and memory.
candidates.reservation: International recognition does not cover the full breadth of the career.

candidates.name: Patrick Chamoiseau
candidates.works: Texaco; Slave Old Man
candidates.rationale: Creolized narrative forms bring oral memory and collective history into the modern novel.
candidates.reservation: Language-specific innovation requires informed evaluation across translations.

candidates.name: Javier Cercas
candidates.works: Soldiers of Salamis; The Anatomy of a Moment
candidates.rationale: Investigative narratives unsettle the boundary between documented history and imaginative reconstruction.
candidates.reservation: The case should distinguish his formal contribution from the importance of Spanish historical debates.

candidates.name: Enrique Vila-Matas
candidates.works: Bartleby & Co.; Dublinesque
candidates.rationale: Metafiction turns the literary life, quotation and failed authorship into inventive narrative engines.
candidates.reservation: The self-referential aesthetic may appear narrower than more socially expansive alternatives.

candidates.name: Antonio Muñoz Molina
candidates.works: Sepharad; In the Night of Time
candidates.rationale: Layered narratives join memory, exile and historical catastrophe through precise prose.
candidates.reservation: A final case needs to encompass the range beyond historical fiction.

candidates.name: Luis Mateo Díez
candidates.works: The Fountain of Age; The Ruin of Heaven
candidates.rationale: A large imagined provincial world joins oral storytelling with grotesque and dreamlike fiction.
candidates.reservation: Limited English availability makes international comparison harder.

candidates.name: Eduardo Mendoza
candidates.works: The Truth About the Savolta Case; The City of Marvels
candidates.rationale: Historical reconstruction and comic experiment recast the social novel of modern Spain.
candidates.reservation: The committee would need to weigh formal range across serious and comic work.

candidates.name: Bernardo Atxaga
candidates.works: Obabakoak; The Accordionist’s Son
candidates.rationale: Inventive storytelling connects Basque language, communal memory and political violence.
candidates.reservation: Self-translation and varying editions complicate identification of the representative corpus.

candidates.name: Jaume Cabré
candidates.works: Confessions; Voices of the Pamano
candidates.rationale: Polyphonic novels connect individual guilt, music and the long afterlife of European violence.
candidates.reservation: The case requires assessment beyond the two most visible translated novels.

candidates.name: Olvido García Valdés
candidates.works: And We Were All Alive; The Dream of the Body
candidates.rationale: An elliptical poetry probes perception, bodily vulnerability and the relation between language and being.
candidates.reservation: Translation is limited and the poetic texture resists brief summaries.

candidates.name: Lídia Jorge
candidates.works: The Murmuring Coast; The Wind Whistling in the Cranes
candidates.rationale: A sustained novelistic oeuvre interrogates colonial memory, gender and changing Portuguese society.
candidates.reservation: The wider corpus is only unevenly represented in English.

candidates.name: Hélia Correia
candidates.works: The Return of Lilias Fraser; Perdition
candidates.rationale: Mythic and theatrical writing connects women’s voices, history and literary inheritance.
candidates.reservation: Limited translation makes genre breadth difficult to compare internationally.

candidates.name: Gonçalo M. Tavares
candidates.works: Jerusalem; Learning to Pray in the Age of Technique
candidates.rationale: Interconnected fictional and philosophical projects examine systems, cruelty and modern rationality.
candidates.reservation: The large, heterogeneous corpus calls for a carefully justified representative selection.

candidates.name: Jenny Erpenbeck
candidates.works: Visitation; Kairos
candidates.rationale: Compressed structures connect intimate relations with state histories and the consequences of political change.
candidates.reservation: The case should extend beyond recent international prize recognition.

candidates.name: Durs Grünbein
candidates.works: Ashes for Breakfast; The Vocation of Poetry
candidates.rationale: A major poetic project connects bodily perception, classical inheritance and modern German history.
candidates.reservation: A fair assessment requires sustained reading of German poetic form.

candidates.name: Lutz Seiler
candidates.works: Kruso; Star 111
candidates.rationale: Poetry and fiction render East German memory through dense attention to voice and material life.
candidates.reservation: The international translated corpus is still relatively narrow.

candidates.name: Botho Strauß
candidates.works: Big and Small; The Young Man
candidates.rationale: Fragmented dramatic and prose forms explore estrangement and the collapse of shared social languages.
candidates.reservation: Political commentary should be evaluated separately from the formal literary achievement.

candidates.name: Christoph Ransmayr
candidates.works: The Last World; The Terrors of Ice and Darkness
candidates.rationale: Mythic and documentary narrative combine to explore catastrophe, exploration and human limits.
candidates.reservation: The committee should compare the wider oeuvre beyond the two early landmark novels.

candidates.name: Arnon Grunberg
candidates.works: Tirza; The Jewish Messiah
candidates.rationale: Darkly comic novels probe humiliation, displacement and the fragility of moral identity.
candidates.reservation: English reception remains incomplete across a prolific career.

candidates.name: Stefan Hertmans
candidates.works: War and Turpentine; The Convert
candidates.rationale: Hybrid historical narratives connect intimate records with the larger pressures of European history.
candidates.reservation: The poetry and earlier prose should not be eclipsed by recent translated novels.

candidates.name: Ludmila Ulitskaya
candidates.works: The Big Green Tent; Daniel Stein, Interpreter
candidates.rationale: Interwoven lives explore dissent, spiritual pluralism and the moral experience of Soviet history.
candidates.reservation: The comparative case should distinguish narrative achievement from political reputation.

candidates.name: Ludmila Petrushevskaya
candidates.works: The Time: Night; There Once Lived a Woman Who Tried to Kill Her Neighbor’s Baby
candidates.rationale: Dark fables, dramatic voices and compressed narratives expose the violence of ordinary domestic life.
candidates.reservation: The international case needs both dramatic and prose corpora.

candidates.name: Vladimir Sorokin
candidates.works: Day of the Oprichnik; Blue Lard
candidates.rationale: Radical stylistic imitation and grotesque speculation expose the literary machinery of authoritarian power.
candidates.reservation: Shock and provocation need to be assessed for their formal necessity.

candidates.name: Mikhail Shishkin
candidates.works: Maidenhair; The Light and the Dark
candidates.rationale: Layered voices and temporal structures connect mortality, language and historical survival.
candidates.reservation: A relatively small novel corpus makes the scale comparison significant.

candidates.name: Maria Stepanova
candidates.works: In Memory of Memory; Holy Winter 20/21
candidates.rationale: Poetry and hybrid historical writing investigate archival absence and the ethics of remembrance.
candidates.reservation: The international case should include the poetry rather than rely chiefly on one prose book.

candidates.name: Yuri Andrukhovych
candidates.works: Perverzion; Moscoviad
candidates.rationale: Carnivalesque prose and poetry challenged Soviet narrative conventions and remade Ukrainian urban imagination.
candidates.reservation: Political urgency should not replace assessment of the long-standing formal achievement.

candidates.name: Oksana Zabuzhko
candidates.works: Fieldwork in Ukrainian Sex; The Museum of Abandoned Secrets
candidates.rationale: Feminist and historical narratives join bodily experience with suppressed cultural memory.
candidates.reservation: Translation gives only partial access to a substantial multigenre oeuvre.

candidates.name: Serhiy Zhadan
candidates.works: Voroshilovgrad; The Orphanage
candidates.rationale: Poetry and fiction transform postindustrial lives and wartime dislocation through distinctive voices.
candidates.reservation: Current visibility should be weighed against the full prewar literary career.

candidates.name: Ewa Lipska
candidates.works: A New Century; Dear Ms. Schubert
candidates.rationale: Ironic, compressed poetry tests the language of social conformity, memory and modern estrangement.
candidates.reservation: Translation offers an incomplete view of a long poetic career.

candidates.name: Ryszard Krynicki
candidates.works: Our Life Is Growing; Magnetic Point
candidates.rationale: A movement toward poetic compression connects linguistic vigilance with historical and ethical pressure.
candidates.reservation: The small-scale, exacting lyric requires assessment in and across the original language.

candidates.name: Drago Jančar
candidates.works: I Saw Her That Night; The Galley Slave
candidates.rationale: Shifting perspectives and historical fiction explore coercion, memory and human agency.
candidates.reservation: International comparison requires more than the most widely translated historical novel.

candidates.name: Slavenka Drakulić
candidates.works: S.: A Novel About the Balkans; The Taste of a Man
candidates.rationale: Fiction and literary essays examine bodily vulnerability, war and ordinary complicity.
candidates.reservation: The balance between fiction and public commentary needs a precise literary case.

candidates.name: Per Petterson
candidates.works: Out Stealing Horses; I Curse the River of Time
candidates.rationale: Restrained narration turns family estrangement and rural memory into concentrated emotional structures.
candidates.reservation: A relatively consistent aesthetic needs comparison for range as well as precision.

candidates.name: Karl Ove Knausgaard
candidates.works: My Struggle; The Morning Star
candidates.rationale: A sustained autobiographical project reconfigured the scale and texture of ordinary-life narration.
candidates.reservation: Self-exposure and volume do not by themselves establish literary innovation.

candidates.name: Sjón
candidates.works: The Blue Fox; Moonstone
candidates.rationale: Compressed, mythic narratives connect folklore, queer lives and historical violence.
candidates.reservation: The poetry and wider Icelandic corpus require assessment alongside translated novellas.

candidates.name: Jón Kalman Stefánsson
candidates.works: Heaven and Hell; Your Absence Is Darkness
candidates.rationale: Lyrical, intergenerational narratives connect harsh environments with love, loss and communal memory.
candidates.reservation: The translated novels should be tested for range beyond a recognizable lyrical register.

candidates.name: Pia Tafdrup
candidates.works: Queen’s Gate; Tarkovsky’s Horses
candidates.rationale: A sustained lyric project makes embodiment, perception and historical memory formally interdependent.
candidates.reservation: The international translated selection remains limited.

candidates.name: Pirkko Saisio
candidates.works: The Red Book of Farewells; Lowest Common Multiple
candidates.rationale: Experimental autobiography and drama connect queer identity, class and Finland’s social transformations.
candidates.reservation: Limited translation complicates evaluation across a substantial multigenre career.

candidates.name: Kerstin Ekman
candidates.works: Blackwater; The Forest of Hours
candidates.rationale: A large novelistic oeuvre joins women’s histories, landscape and ecological time with narrative invention.
candidates.reservation: Former Swedish Academy membership requires explicit consideration in a simulation of Academy preferences.

candidates.name: Tua Forsström
candidates.works: Snow Leopard; After Having Spent a Night Among Horses
candidates.rationale: Concentrated lyric and associative sequences connect grief, nature and the instability of perception.
candidates.reservation: Former Swedish Academy membership and limited translation require explicit contextual review.

candidates.name: César Aira
candidates.works: An Episode in the Life of a Landscape Painter; The Literary Conference
candidates.rationale: A prolific sequence of short novels makes improvisation and abrupt transformation into a distinctive literary method.
candidates.reservation: The huge, uneven corpus complicates any representative selection.

candidates.name: Luisa Valenzuela
candidates.works: The Lizard’s Tail; He Who Searches
candidates.rationale: Experimental fiction exposes the relation between political terror, sexuality and narrative authority.
candidates.reservation: International circulation covers only part of a long career.

candidates.name: Samanta Schweblin
candidates.works: Fever Dream; Little Eyes
candidates.rationale: Compressed, unsettling narratives give technological and ecological anxiety unusual formal precision.
candidates.reservation: A comparatively short career leaves the lifetime-achievement question open.

candidates.name: Raúl Zurita
candidates.works: Purgatory; The Country of Planks
candidates.rationale: Large poetic sequences and landscape-scale interventions transform suffering into collective memorial form.
candidates.reservation: Performance and visual dimensions require assessment beyond printed translation.

candidates.name: Diamela Eltit
candidates.works: E. Luminata; The Fourth World
candidates.rationale: Radical narrative structures connect bodily experience with dictatorship and social exclusion.
candidates.reservation: A demanding, partially translated corpus makes comparative reading difficult.

candidates.name: Nona Fernández
candidates.works: The Twilight Zone; Space Invaders
candidates.rationale: Fragmented narratives connect intimate memory with the erased lives of dictatorship.
candidates.reservation: International recognition rests on a relatively small translated portion of the oeuvre.

candidates.name: Cristina Peri Rossi
candidates.works: The Ship of Fools; State of Exile
candidates.rationale: A multigenre oeuvre joins exile, desire and political displacement through inventive narrative and lyric forms.
candidates.reservation: The poetry and stories need as much attention as the best-known novel.

candidates.name: Ida Vitale
candidates.works: Pre-texts; Byobu
candidates.rationale: Exacting lyric and prose miniatures explore language, perception and the intellectual life of exile.
candidates.reservation: Age warrants a current status check; translation conveys only part of the poetic texture.

candidates.name: Elena Poniatowska
candidates.works: Massacre in Mexico; Here’s to You, Jesusa!
candidates.rationale: Documentary polyphony gives marginalized lives a powerful place in Mexican literary history.
candidates.reservation: The ethical mediation of others’ testimony deserves direct assessment.

candidates.name: Margo Glantz
candidates.works: The Family Tree; The Wake
candidates.rationale: Fragmented autobiographical and critical writing joins migration, the body and cultural memory.
candidates.reservation: A dispersed, cross-genre oeuvre makes representative reading difficult.

candidates.name: Cristina Rivera Garza
candidates.works: No One Will See Me Cry; Liliana’s Invincible Summer
candidates.rationale: Experimental fiction and archival writing question authorship, violence and the recovery of erased lives.
candidates.reservation: The comparative case should encompass the fiction alongside recent acclaimed nonfiction.

candidates.name: Carmen Boullosa
candidates.works: They’re Cows, We’re Pigs; Before
candidates.rationale: Inventive historical and fantastical narratives recast colonial power and women’s experience.
candidates.reservation: English translation provides an incomplete view of a very broad oeuvre.

candidates.name: Homero Aridjis
candidates.works: Solar Poems; 1492: The Life and Times of Juan Cabezón of Castile
candidates.rationale: Poetry and historical fiction connect ecological imagination, myth and the lives displaced by history.
candidates.reservation: Environmental prominence should be separated from the sustained literary case.

candidates.name: Gonzalo Celorio
candidates.works: And Let the Earth Tremble at Its Centers; Three Pretty Cubans
candidates.rationale: Urban narrative and family memory join intimate histories with Mexican and Caribbean cultural experience.
candidates.reservation: International translation and reception are relatively limited.

candidates.name: Laura Restrepo
candidates.works: Delirium; The Dark Bride
candidates.rationale: Layered narrative voices connect political violence with intimate and psychological disorder.
candidates.reservation: The case needs a comparative account of formal range across the oeuvre.

candidates.name: Piedad Bonnett
candidates.works: What Has No Name; The Wretches
candidates.rationale: Poetry and autobiographical prose connect grief, mental illness and ordinary social violence.
candidates.reservation: The internationally visible nonfiction should not eclipse the poetry.

candidates.name: Sergio Ramírez
candidates.works: Margarita, How Beautiful the Sea; Divine Punishment
candidates.rationale: Historical and civic narratives combine irony, documentary detail and the social worlds of Central America.
candidates.reservation: Political stature should be weighed separately from the novelistic achievement.

candidates.name: Gioconda Belli
candidates.works: The Inhabited Woman; The Country Under My Skin
candidates.rationale: A long multigenre oeuvre joins erotic autonomy, revolutionary history and women’s political experience.
candidates.reservation: The committee should distinguish formal achievement from public and political symbolism.

candidates.name: Leonardo Padura
candidates.works: The Man Who Loved Dogs; Heretics
candidates.rationale: Crime and historical narratives use investigative structures to examine disillusionment and displaced memory.
candidates.reservation: A literary case must encompass the work beyond the prestige of historical subjects.

candidates.name: Reina María Rodríguez
candidates.works: The Winter Garden; The Varieties of the Real World
candidates.rationale: An intimate, materially attentive lyric transforms scarcity, memory and urban experience.
candidates.reservation: Limited translation and a specialized reception make the comparison demanding.

candidates.name: Raduan Nassar
candidates.works: Ancient Tillage; A Cup of Rage
candidates.rationale: Intense rhythmic prose transforms family, desire and authority within a small but influential corpus.
candidates.reservation: The exceptionally small oeuvre makes breadth the clearest comparative question.

candidates.name: Adélia Prado
candidates.works: The Alphabet in the Park; Ex-Voto
candidates.rationale: A distinctive lyric joins ordinary domestic life with embodied spirituality and desire.
candidates.reservation: A current status check and wider Portuguese reading are needed beyond English selections.

candidates.name: Conceição Evaristo
candidates.works: Ponciá Vicêncio; Olhos d’Água
candidates.rationale: Interlinked memory and voice give Black Brazilian women’s experiences a distinctive literary form.
candidates.reservation: The committee should establish formal achievement across works beyond their social importance.

candidates.name: Milton Hatoum
candidates.works: The Brothers; Tale of a Certain Orient
candidates.rationale: Layered family narratives connect Amazonian spaces, migration and the instability of memory.
candidates.reservation: The internationally visible corpus remains relatively compact.

candidates.name: Chico Buarque
candidates.works: Budapest; Spilt Milk
candidates.rationale: Unreliable narrative voices and lyrical work explore class, desire and historical self-deception.
candidates.reservation: The award case should state how fiction, theatre and song lyrics contribute to the literary oeuvre.
